correctness.rationale: The random cyclic anchor makes all circular spacings Dirichlet(1,...,1). Conditioning on a clockwise r-gap partial sum Beta(r,n-r) and reweighting the disjoint opposing gap produces a Beta(r,n-r+1) order-statistic integral; a centered binomial absolute-moment identity gives Delta_n=1/4−2^(−n−1)binom(n,(n−1)/2) for odd n. Uniform deletion from even n preserves iid uniform remaining locations and adds an independent omitted agent with conditional mean distance 1/4, yielding Delta_(n−1). The empirical circle cost process H_n(t)=sqrt(n)(average d(X_i,t)−1/4) has bounded fourth increments and finite-dimensional Gaussian limit in C(T), covariance 1/48−h²/2+2h³/3. Its exact antipodal symmetry implies sup G=−inf G>0 almost surely. The PCD/EPCD opposing-gap selection measures converge weakly to Haar uniformly in continuous test functions; tightness of H_n upgrades their integrals to o_P(1). Therefore all conditional selected costs equal n/4+o_P(sqrt(n)), while optimum equals n/4+sqrt(n)min H_n, giving the common joint 4 sup G limit and non-Gaussian positive law. Independent exact rational identity checks reproduced Delta_3=1/16, Delta_5=3/32, Delta_7=29/256, Delta_9=65/512. Numerical Monte Carlo in the checker is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact finite-population expected gain is a natural performance metric under a homogeneous input distribution and distinguishes lotteries whose worst-case guarantees differ. The non-Gaussian Gaussian-supremum law quantifies the first stochastic order of approximation inefficiency and shows three mechanism ratios share a fluctuation limit despite distinct unconditional costs. This is a motivated concrete mechanism-specific comparison, not merely a general empirical-process exercise.

final_claim: For n>=3 Haar-uniform independent circle agents, Random Dictator minus Proportional Circle Distance/Even PCD expected social cost equals 1/4−binom(s,(s−1)/2)/2^(s+1), s=n if odd and n−1 if even; the equal mixture has half gain. Their conditional expected-cost approximation ratios share the joint non-Gaussian limit sqrt(n)(R_n^M−1) -> 4 sup G, with explicit covariance 1/48−h²/2+2h³/3.
